question.text: If two vectors <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>P</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mi>m</mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>  and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>Q</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mi>m</mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>  are perpendicular to each other. Then, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> will be

solution.text:
For two vectors to be perpendicular, their dot product is equal to zero.

So, P→·Q→=0

⇒i^+2mj^+mk^·4i^-2j^+mk^=0⇒4-4m+m2=0⇒m-22=0⇒m=2
